label: input z/j/y near the <DEL> boundary in long sequences
explanation: Token-gated unit: about 95% of activations (96% of mass) fall on steps whose input is one of z, j, y, h, f, p, with z by far the strongest (46% of mass, 12.7x lift), then j and y. It never fires at t<=2 or on the <DEL> step, and fires mostly late, at t>=6. It concentrates around the delimiter: the last one or two original tokens (orig_idx 7-8 has the highest rate) and the first copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. re-inputting orig(0)/orig(1), 52% of mass). The top activations are almost all z re-fed at recall_idx 1 in L>=8 sequences. Rate and magnitude grow with sequence length L (L=9 holds 49% of mass). It does NOT fire on most occurrences of these tokens: even z at recall_idx 1 is active only ~45% of the time, so some unmodeled hidden-state context also matters. Precision is the main gap.
